* A devastating Russian bomb attack struck Ukraine’s north-eastern city of Kharkiv, leaving seven people dead and injuring at least 77 others, according to local authorities. Among the victims was a 14-year-old girl, reported Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskiy. The strike hit both a residential building and a playground, leaving significant destruction in its wake and causing major panic among local residents.  
* The death toll rose to seven after rescuers recovered a woman’s body from the rubble, and regional governor Oleh Syniehubov stated that around 20 of the injured remain in severe condition. Ukrainian officials identified that five aerial guided “glide bombs” were launched from planes stationed in Russia’s Belgorod region, targeting the city with precision.  
* In response, President Zelenskiy renewed his call for Ukraine’s western allies to grant control over the use of long-range western weapons so Ukraine’s forces could strike Russian military airbases where these attacks originate. He argued that better access to advanced medium- and long-range systems would enable Ukraine to protect its cities and civilians effectively, reinforcing the need for comprehensive support. Zelenskiy emphasized, “There is no rational reason to restrict Ukraine’s defences,” urging international partners to reconsider current limitations.  
* Meanwhile, Russia claimed Ukraine fired cluster munitions at the Russian city of Belgorod and its suburbs, an attack that left at least five people dead and 37 wounded, including six children. Regional governor Vyacheslav Gladkov detailed that “one woman and four men died of their wounds on the spot before an ambulance arrived,” and he uploaded footage of a burning house believed to have been hit during the barrage.  
* The ongoing conflict has led to extensive damage to local infrastructure, disrupting mobile and other forms of communication. Residents reported difficulty in reaching emergency services as mobile reception suffered, especially in areas close to the destroyed tower blocks. Both sides accuse the other of escalating the conflict and failing to protect civilians, while people in Kharkiv and Belgorod struggle to regain a sense of normalcy amidst mounting casualties and growing fears of further attacks. The destruction of a key communication tower in Kharkiv has further hampered rescue operations and coordination efforts, underlining the urgent need for effective control over both defensive and communication technologies in conflict zones.
